author: Yadunandan Mandalaneni
note: Learning style describes the training objective, not a permanent property of an architecture. Broad supervised/unsupervised categories appear alongside the specific training setup. In self-supervised training, targets come from the data itself. Conditional models and later fine-tuning can add supervision. Domain labels show selected common uses, not every possible application. All use cases are illustrative, not reported experiments.

algorithms.name: Linear Regression
algorithms.how: Fits a weighted linear relationship between input features and a numeric target.
algorithms.use: Estimate a home price from area, location features, and property characteristics.
algorithms.cue: Start with an interpretable numeric baseline; inspect residuals and assumptions.

algorithms.name: Random Forest
algorithms.how: Trains randomized decision trees on resampled data, then averages predictions or votes.
algorithms.use: Predict customer churn from account activity and service history.
algorithms.cue: Captures nonlinear patterns; individual predictions are harder to explain than one tree.

algorithms.name: Gradient Boosting
algorithms.how: Adds weak learners sequentially, each improving the current ensemble against a chosen loss.
algorithms.use: Rank loan applications by default risk using labeled historical outcomes.
algorithms.cue: Useful for structured prediction; tune complexity to control overfitting.

algorithms.name: Convolutional Neural Network
algorithms.how: Learns shared local filters and progressively combines visual features to predict a class.
algorithms.use: Flag visible manufacturing defects in labeled product photographs.
algorithms.cue: Learns image features; performance depends on representative images and labels.

algorithms.name: K-Means
algorithms.how: Alternates assigning points to the closest centroid and updating each cluster mean.
algorithms.use: Group customers by scaled purchasing behavior without predefined segment labels.
algorithms.cue: Choose k and scale features; compact clusters may miss complex shapes.

algorithms.name: Principal Component Analysis
algorithms.how: Projects centered data onto orthogonal directions that retain the most variance.
algorithms.use: Reduce correlated sensor measurements to fewer features for visualization.
algorithms.cue: Compresses features, not clusters; high variance need not mean task relevance.

algorithms.name: BERT
algorithms.how: Uses bidirectional context to recover masked tokens; original BERT also used a sentence-pair objective.
algorithms.use: Fine-tune a pretrained encoder on labeled support tickets to classify intent.
algorithms.cue: The ticket classifier is supervised fine-tuning; BERT is not a free-form text generator.

algorithms.name: GPT-style Transformer
algorithms.how: Uses causal attention to predict the next token from preceding tokens, then generates sequentially.
algorithms.use: Draft a product description from a supplied brief, followed by human review.
algorithms.cue: Base pretraining is shown; later instruction tuning can add other learning styles.

algorithms.name: Generative Adversarial Network
algorithms.how: A generator synthesizes samples while a discriminator learns to distinguish generated from real data.
algorithms.use: Generate synthetic product-image variations for creative exploration.
algorithms.cue: Training can be unstable or collapse to limited outputs; conditional variants add supervision.

algorithms.name: Diffusion Model
algorithms.how: Learns to reverse added noise; repeated denoising transforms a random sample into generated content.
algorithms.use: Generate image concepts; text-conditioned variants guide generation with prompts.
algorithms.cue: The baseline needs no human class labels; text-image conditioning uses paired information.

comparisons: Both combine trees for labeled prediction. A forest averages randomized trees to reduce variance. Boosting builds learners sequentially to improve a loss. Compare both with the same validation split; neither is automatically best. [10]
K-Means assigns observations to groups. PCA creates new continuous feature directions. PCA may precede clustering, but retained variance alone does not show that useful groups exist. [1, 11]

BERT uses bidirectional context to learn representations. A task head can classify a complete text. A GPT-style base model uses preceding context to predict and generate the next token. Both can be adapted after pretraining. [3, 4]
scenario: Past sales and known features -> predicted units. Compare MAE/RMSE on a later time period and against a simple demand baseline. [8, 9]
Scaled purchasing features -> candidate groups. Check stability, separation, and business usefulness; groups are not established customer truths. [1, 11]
Ticket text plus intent labels -> intent class. Use per-class precision/recall and macro-F1; inspect errors on similar or rare intents. [3, 8]
Brief -> draft text; noise or conditioning -> image candidates. Review prompt adherence, factual accuracy for text, image quality, and output diversity. [4-6]
